What happens if there aren't enough consecutive hours for that particular day, and if the data does not cover a range of 24 hours (the original definition of RA spans 24 hours I believe) ? Is it reported as a NaN then?

Thank you for all your hard work!

Mayank

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR Part5 – Incomplete 24h days not included in summary
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GGIR Part5 – Incomplete 24h days not included in summary
messages.body_plain:
This is intentional, including incomplete days when doing time use analysis, as part 5 does, will bias your results.

Possible solutions:
Analyse data from wake-up to wake-up or from sleep onset to sleep onset which may align better with the start and end time of your study compared with midnight-midnight  day windows. https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter12_TimeUseAnalysis.html
For future studies: Collect more days of data. I think at least N + 3 days of data if you want to quantify behaviour across a N day period. One of the major limitations of for example UK Biobank accelerometer data is that it was collected over only 7x24 hours making it impossible to reliably quantify both sleep and day time activity for 7 consecutive days.
 <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter12_TimeUseAnalysis.html>
That said, I think you missed parameter minimum_MM_length.part5 <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#minimum_mm_length-part5> which is a way to make GGIR a bit more tolerant to incomplete days when working with midnight-midnight (MM) windows, but as I mentioned above this would introduce bias if not done carefully. For example, you can only use it if you are convinced that the missing data on those days is reflected by time spent in behavioural classes that are not used in your research. I think this is very tricky and I would advise against it.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.body_plain:
Hi Kelsey and Audrey,

The average acceleration cannot be calculated if no time is spent in a behavioural class. The missing value is not a bug but intentional.

See also my response to the same question from last year: https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/4-9_SiMtwcU/m/M61FsMRiAQAJ

The essence is that working with units of time requires a different interpretation than working with units of acceleration. Zero time spent in a behaviour always has a meaning, even if a person never spends time in it, while zero acceleration only has meaning if a person actually participants in a behaviour.

Best,

Vincent

I am new to GGIR and have encountered an issue that seems to be similar to what others have reported recently in this group. I’m hoping someone can provide some clarity on the matter.

We are using GGIR package version 3.2 to analyze accelerometer data from Actigraph GT3X-BT devices. Study participants have been instructed to wear the accelerometer on their non-dominant wrist for 3 weeks, 24/7, only taking it off during water-based activities.

In both the cleaned daysummary (part5_daysummary_MM_L44.8M100.6V428.8_T5A5) and full daysummay report (part5_daysummary_full_MM_L44.8M100.6V428.8_T5A5), we have observed unexpected values for the dur_day_spt_min variable. Since we are working with midnight-to-midnight reports, we would expect all values for dur_day_spt_min to be 1440 minutes (24 hours). Although most of the full windows in our output files are 1440 minutes, some deviate in both the cleaned and full daysummary.

Specifically, 14 of the days present in part5_daysummary_MM_L44.8M100.6V428.8_T5A5 are longer than 1440 minutes (ranging from 1500 to 3720 minutes). Additionally, three days show durations shorter than expected (each is 1380 minutes). The report contains nearly 900 days, so this issue does not occur for every participant. Furthermore, it tends to affect the first or last window of the measurement period.

I have attached the script we have been using for reference.

We are unsure how to interpret these results or whether something went wrong during the analysis. Any advice on this issue would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you in advance!

Emilia

Hi Mayank,

GGIR does not calculate RA. I assumed that GGIR users would be able to calculate it themselves from the GGIR output. Maybe in the future RA can be added.

GGIR allows you to ignore days with insufficient valid data, which I think addresses your concern.

Please note that postGGIR has been developed by Wei Guo and colleagues, and later renamed to mMARCH.AC: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mMARCH.AC/index.html
If you have questions about their package I encourage you to reach out to them.

Best, Vincent

If free living data would work, we might be able to help with this.

Best,
Jenny Moreno

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I’m currently working with GGIR for accelerometer data analysis and would greatly appreciate your expertise. Specifically, I’m trying to extract lux data from Axivity accelerometers using GGIR. The data is in CSV format, which was converted from a parquet file.

I’ve included my code below for reference. If anyone has experience with this or can offer guidance on how to proceed, your input would be invaluable!

GGIR(
  # Basic parameters
  mode = c(1,2,3,4,5,6),
  outputdir = outputdir,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  do.parallel = TRUE,
  do.report = c(2, 4, 5, 6),

  #=====================
  # read.myacc.csv arguments
  #=====================
  rmc.nrow = Inf,
  rmc.dec = ".",
  rmc.firstrow.acc = 2,
  rmc.col.acc = 2:4,
  rmc.col.time = 1,
  rmc.unit.acc = "g",
  rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",
  rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
  rmc.sf = 12.5,
  desiredtz = "Australia/Melbourne",

  # Part 1
  windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
  do.cal = TRUE,
  do.enmo = TRUE,
  do.anglex = TRUE,
  do.angley = TRUE,
  do.anglez = TRUE,

  #=====================
  # Part 2
  #=====================
  dayborder = 0,
  data_masking_strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 0,
  hrs.del.end = 0,
  maxdur = 0,
  includedaycrit = 16,
  do.imp = TRUE,

  #=====================
  # Part 3 + 4
  #=====================
  ignorenonwear = FALSE,
  do.part3.pdf = FALSE,
  HASPT.algo = "HDCZA",                     # SPT-window detection for wrist
  HASIB.algo = "vanHees2015",               # SIB algorithm for wrist
  anglethreshold = c(5,10),             # Angle threshold in degrees
  timethreshold = c(5,10),              # Time threshold in minutes
  includenightcrit = 16,          # Minimum hours for valid night
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  do.visual = TRUE,
  outliers.only = FALSE,
  loglocation= c(),

  LUX_day_segments = c(1,2,3,4,5,6, 12, 18,20,21,22,23,24),

  #=====================
  # Part 5
  #=====================
  acc.metric = "ENMO",
  threshold.lig = c(44.8),
  threshold.mod = c(100.6),
  threshold.vig = c(428.8),
  boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,
  boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
  boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,20,30),
  boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),
  excludefirstlast.part5 = FALSE,
  save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE,
  save_ms5raw_format = "csv",
  save_ms5raw_without_invalid = TRUE,

  #=====================
  # Part 6
  #=====================
  winhr = c(5, 10),
  cosinor = TRUE,
  part6CR = TRUE,
  part6Window = c("start","end"),

  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
  timewindow = c("OO","MM"),
  visualreport = TRUE,
  old_visualreport = FALSE
)

Thank you!

Best regards,
Rosalind
